title: Simplify install.sh: hardcode repo, remove dead schedule code, drop all sed
body:
## Context

Running `install.sh` on macOS fails with:
```
sed: 1: ".github/workflows/versi ...": invalid command code .
```

BSD sed requires `sed -i ''` vs GNU sed's `sed -i`. But deeper analysis shows the sed calls are either dead code (schedule substitution against templates that don't have the placeholder) or unnecessary complexity (SEMVER_REPO param for hypothetical forks).

## Acceptance Criteria

### install.sh changes
- [ ] Remove the `SEMVER_REPO` parameter — script takes only `<version>`
- [ ] Remove all schedule/cron code (lines 52-70: read/validate, lines 88-91: sed substitute) — dead code, templates have no schedule placeholder
- [ ] Remove all `sed` calls from `install_workflow()` — no substitution needed
- [ ] Update usage comment and header to reflect single-param interface
- [ ] `install_workflow()` just fetches the template, no post-processing

### Template changes
- [ ] `templates/github/workflows/install-git-semver.yml`: change `SEMVER_REPO: USER/git-semver` to `SEMVER_REPO: mangimangi/git-semver`

### README changes
- [ ] Remove `install.schedule` from config docs (line ~165, ~209)
- [ ] Remove "Runs weekly to check for updates" mention (line ~28)
- [ ] Simplify install command examples to `bash -s <version>` (drop repo param)

### Workflow changes
- [ ] Update `.github/workflows/install-git-semver.yml` (the repo's own workflow) to pass only version to install.sh (drop repo param from `bash -s` call)
- [ ] Update `.github/workflows/install-on-release.yml` if it also passes repo param

### Tests
- [ ] Add `tests/test_install.sh` (shell tests) or `tests/test_install.py` (pytest) that verify:
  - install.sh creates `.semver/git-semver`, `.semver/.version`, `.semver/config.json`
  - install.sh installs workflow templates when not present
  - install.sh skips workflow templates when already present
  - Installed workflow templates contain `mangimangi/git-semver` (not placeholder)

title: Create .semver/bump-and-release script with tests
body:
## Summary

Move all orchestration logic from `version-bump.yml` into a new `.semver/bump-and-release` Python script. The workflow currently contains ~100 lines of inline bash handling config reading, 4 conditional bump modes (push/dispatch × automerge/PR), PR creation, and release creation. All of this should live in an updatable script so the workflow can be installed once and never modified.

## Design

**Separate script** (not a git-semver subcommand) — keeps `git-semver` CI-agnostic. Follows existing pattern (`.vendored/install`, `.vendored/check`, `.dogfood/resolve`).

The script receives GitHub context via environment variables:
- `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` — "push" or "workflow_dispatch" (built-in GHA var)
- `GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE` — the before SHA for push events (workflow passes this)
- `GITHUB_SHA` — current commit SHA (built-in GHA var)
- `INPUT_BUMP_TYPE` — patch/minor/major (workflow passes from inputs)
- `INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY` — optional subdir (workflow passes from inputs)
- `INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION` — optional changelog text (workflow passes from inputs)
- `GH_TOKEN` — GitHub token (set by workflow)
- `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` — owner/repo (built-in GHA var)

### Logic to move from workflow

1. **Read config** — extract `install.on_merge` and `install.automerge` from `.semver/config.json`
2. **Git user config** — set github-actions[bot] name/email
3. **Push + automerge=true** — `.semver/git-semver bump-all --since $BEFORE`
4. **Push + automerge=false** — bump-all --no-push, create PR if changes detected
5. **Dispatch + automerge=true** — `.semver/git-semver bump $TYPE [--subdir] [--description]`
6. **Dispatch + automerge=false** — bump --no-push, create PR
7. **Release creation** — iterate tags at HEAD, `gh release create` for each

### Exit behavior
- Exit 0 on success (including "nothing to bump")
- Exit 1 on error

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `.semver/bump-and-release` script exists and is executable
- [ ] Handles all 4 bump modes (push/dispatch × automerge/PR) matching current workflow behavior exactly
- [ ] Handles release creation for tags at HEAD
- [ ] Reads config from `.semver/config.json` for on_merge/automerge
- [ ] Respects on_merge=false (skips push-triggered bumps)
- [ ] Sets git user config (github-actions[bot])
- [ ] New test file `tests/test_bump_and_release.py` covering:
  - Config reading (on_merge/automerge defaults and overrides)
  - Push + automerge mode (calls bump-all with --since)
  - Push + PR mode (calls bump-all --no-push, creates branch/PR when changes detected)
  - Dispatch + automerge mode (calls bump with correct args)
  - Dispatch + PR mode (calls bump --no-push, creates branch/PR)
  - Release creation (iterates tags, calls gh release create)
  - No-op when on_merge=false and event=push
- [ ] `.semver/config.json` updated: add `bump-and-release` to `files` array (triggers auto patch bump on changes)

title: Slim version-bump.yml workflow and update install.sh
body:
## Summary

Replace the logic-heavy `version-bump.yml` workflow with a thin shell that delegates to `.semver/bump-and-release`. Update `install.sh` to deliver the new script. Update the template workflow.

## Changes

### 1. `templates/github/workflows/version-bump.yml`
The template workflow becomes a thin shell:
- Keep: name, triggers, permissions, concurrency, checkout step, job-level `if` for skip conditions
- Replace: all inline bash steps → single step that sets env vars and calls `.semver/bump-and-release`
- The workflow passes GitHub-specific context (event.before, inputs) as env vars

### 2. `.github/workflows/version-bump.yml` (this repo's own copy)
Update to match the new template. This repo dogfoods itself so both must be consistent.

### 3. `install.sh`
Add download of `bump-and-release` script alongside `git-semver`:
```bash
fetch_file "bump-and-release" ".semver/bump-and-release"
chmod +x .semver/bump-and-release
```

### 4. Vendor protection
Update `.vendored/config.json` if needed — the `.semver/**` glob already covers `.semver/bump-and-release`, so no change may be needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `templates/github/workflows/version-bump.yml` is a thin workflow (~40 lines) that calls `.semver/bump-and-release`
- [ ] `.github/workflows/version-bump.yml` matches the template
- [ ] `install.sh` downloads and installs `bump-and-release` alongside `git-semver`
- [ ] Workflow passes all required env vars: `GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE`, `INPUT_BUMP_TYPE`, `INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY`, `INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION`
- [ ] Built-in GHA vars (`GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`, `GITHUB_SHA`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GH_TOKEN`) are available without explicit passing
- [ ] `.vendored/config.json` protection still covers the new script (`.semver/**` glob)
- [ ] No functional regression — the new workflow + script produces identical behavior to the old workflow

title: Add _vendor self-registration to config template
body:
Follow-up to gsv-9ed5 (Vendor V2 Contract Compliance).

When install.sh creates .vendored/configs/git-semver.json on first install, it fetches templates/semver/config.json which lacks _vendor metadata. The framework needs this block for protected/allowed path enforcement.

Update templates/semver/config.json to include:

```json
"_vendor": {
  "repo": "mangimangi/git-semver",
  "install_branch": "chore/install-git-semver",
  "protected": [".vendored/pkg/git-semver/**", ".github/workflows/version-bump.yml"],
  "allowed": [".vendored/configs/git-semver.json"]
}
```

Acceptance criteria:
- templates/semver/config.json includes _vendor block with correct protected/allowed paths
- No sed/substitution needed — all values are static
- Existing repos unaffected (create-only guard in install.sh)
- Delete docs/planning/vendor-self-registration.md after implementation (knowledge migrated to issue)

title: tag --push fails when only one component bumped in monorepo
body:
In a monorepo with root + subdirectory components, 'git-semver tag --push' tries to create tags for ALL components, not just the one that was bumped. When only one component bumped, the other component's tag already exists at a prior commit and fails with 'Tag X already exists at commit Y, but HEAD is Z'.

Fix: skip tagging a component if a tag for its current VERSION already exists (at any commit). Only create tags for components whose version was actually bumped in this commit.

Acceptance criteria:
- Bumping only root in a monorepo creates only the root tag, skips subdir tags
- Bumping only a subdir creates only the subdir tag, skips root tag
- bump-all that bumps both still creates both tags
- Existing tests pass, new test covers the skip-existing case

title: Git-semver files audit
body:
# Git-semver files audit

> Epic: `mdci-dev-2153` (orchestrator), per-repo plan for `git-semver`

## Problem

The `.vendored/configs/git-semver.json` configuration may be missing entries for user-facing shipped files — command MDs, mode files, doc files, and other artifacts that should trigger a version bump when changed. Missing entries mean changes to these files don't bump the version, leading to stale version numbers that don't reflect actual changes.

## In scope for this repo

Audit `.vendored/configs/git-semver.json` in this repo:

1. Identify all user-facing shipped files: command MDs, mode files, doc files, and any other files that end users or downstream consumers interact with
2. Compare against the current `files` entries in git-semver.json
3. Add any missing file patterns that should trigger version bumps
4. Remove any stale patterns that reference files no longer present

## Reference context (handled elsewhere)

- The same audit is being performed independently in all 6 repos (pearls, madreperla, medici, git-vendored, git-semver, git-dogfood) under this epic. Each repo's audit is self-contained.

## Acceptance criteria

1. All user-facing shipped files are covered by git-semver.json file patterns
2. No stale patterns referencing non-existent files
3. `git-semver check` passes with the updated config

## Out of scope

- Changing git-semver's behavior or configuration schema
- Adding new file types not currently shipped

## Risk notes

- Overly broad glob patterns could trigger unnecessary version bumps on non-user-facing changes. Prefer specific patterns over wildcards where practical.

title: git-semver's own pull request checks run through git-cicd
body:
Unit 2 of plan `git-dev-883c` (record: `mangimangi/git-dev`, `.pearls/docs/epics/git-dev-883c.md`), agreed with the owner on 2026-11-28. Delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`.

## What happens today

git-semver's pull request checks are two hand-written GitHub Actions workflows:

- `.github/workflows/test.yml` ("Tests"): on pull requests, sets up Python `3.x`, `pip install pytest pytest-cov pyyaml`, runs pytest on `tests/`. No Python version was ever chosen: `3.x` is whatever is newest, and `pyproject.toml` declares no `requires-python` at all.
- `.github/workflows/check-vendor.yml` ("Check Vendor Files"): on every pull request, `python3 .vendored/check` with full history. It is installed and protected by git-vendored.

git-cicd v0.0.3 is installed (`.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/`, `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` with no jobs; pull request #91), but the install delivered no `.github/workflows/git-cicd-open.yml`: an install pull request never carries workflow files. So nothing runs through git-cicd yet.

## Required behaviour

git-semver's own pull request checks are declared as git-cicd jobs and run through it, the way git-cicd's own repository does (`mangimangi/git-cicd`: `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json`, `ci/setup.sh`, `ci/test.sh`, README "The config" and "Installing").

- `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` declares an `open` job for the tests, with a setup script that installs what the suite needs on the Python floor the repository declares and a step that runs it, and an `open` job whose step is `.vendored/check`. `paths` and `needs_nothing` are chosen so documents and tracker records need no job.
- The generated workflow exists: `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd generate` is run and `.github/workflows/git-cicd-open.yml` committed (it is listed as editable for the vendor check).
- No Python version is written in any workflow; `pyproject.toml` declares `requires-python`, and it is the floor the tests actually pass on, found by running them on it.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` is removed.
- `AGENTS.md` and `README.md` say how the checks run here (`.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup`, then `check`).

Do not add, change or delete a vendor-protected file: `check-vendor.yml`, `version-bump.yml`, `install-vendored.yml`, `dogfood.yml` and everything a manifest under `.vendored/manifests/` lists stay as they are. The vendor check runs twice for now (the old workflow and the new job); the planning session removes the old one later. Run `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` before finishing and undo anything it reports.

## Acceptance criteria

- The pull request into `plan/git-dev-883c` shows `Open / <name> / git-semver:<job>` rows for the test job and the vendor check job, `Open / Decide / git-cicd:decide`, `Open / Report / git-cicd:report`, and the commit status `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict` is success. The status is a commit status, not a check run: read it from the commit's statuses.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd validate` prints `config ok: 2 jobs` (or more), and `verify` passes.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes in a clean checkout.
- The tests pass on the Python version `requires-python` names as the floor, shown by the job's setup installing that version.
- `.github/workflows/test.yml` no longer exists; no other file under `.github/workflows/` except `git-cicd-open.yml` is changed.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

title: Release is one step: release decides bump or publish itself, and runs as a git-cicd job
release: one entry point that decides bump, publish or nothing for a merge or manual run
body:
## Goal
Running `release` with no subcommand works out which case it is in and does it, so neither a workflow file nor a per-repo script (like git-cicd's `ci/release.sh` in `mangimangi/git-cicd`) has to hold the bump-vs-publish decision. The same script serves a git-cicd job and the existing `.github/workflows/version-bump.yml`. Planning doc: `.pearls/docs/epics/gsv-81b6.md` (unit 4 of plan `git-dev-883c`; delivers into branch `plan/git-dev-883c`).

## Current code (validated against `release`, 259 lines, 2026-11-28)
- `main()` (line 243): `len(sys.argv) < 2` prints `Usage: semver <bump|publish>` and exits 1; `bump` -> `cmd_bump()`, `publish` -> `cmd_publish()`, else exits 1.
- `cmd_bump()` (line 214): reads `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`; `push` -> skips with `on_merge is false, skipping` when `install.on_merge` is false, else `handle_push_bump(automerge)`; `workflow_dispatch` -> `handle_dispatch_bump(automerge)`; other -> `Unknown event`, exit 1.
- `cmd_publish()` (line 233): `configure_git()`, `sync_branch()`, `git_semver("tag", "--push")`, `create_releases()`.
- `handle_push_bump(automerge)` (line 141): requires `GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE` (error + exit 1 if unset); `configure_git`, `sync_branch` (fast-forward to pick up bumps from queued runs), `git-semver bump-all --since <before> --no-push`; returns when HEAD did not move (no bump needed); `automerge: false` -> `create_pr` from `chore/bump-version-<int(time.time())>`; else `try_push_or_pr` (direct push, falls back to PR on `GH006`/protected-branch error) and when the direct push worked, `git-semver tag --push` + `create_releases()` in the same run (a push with the workflow token starts no new run, so publish would never fire).
- `handle_dispatch_bump(automerge)` (line 175): `INPUT_BUMP_TYPE` (default `patch`), `INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY`, `INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION`.
- `read_config()` (line 51): `install.on_merge`, `install.automerge`.
- `sync_branch()` (line 73): branch from `GITHUB_REF` (default `refs/heads/main`).
- `create_releases()` (line 128): `git tag --points-at HEAD`, skips `latest`, `gh release create <tag> --repo $GITHUB_REPOSITORY --title <tag> --generate-notes`.
- The rule being moved in lives today in `version-bump.yml`: job `bump` runs on `workflow_dispatch` or on a push whose head commit message starts with neither `chore: bump version` nor `chore: install`; job `publish` runs on a push whose head commit message starts with `chore: bump version`.

## What to build
A new no-argument path in `main()` (e.g. `cmd_auto()`), reusing the existing handlers:
1. Determine the trigger. If `CICD_TRIGGER` is set, use it: `merge` or `manual`. Otherwise map `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`: `push` -> merge, `workflow_dispatch` -> manual. Any other value (`open`, `cron`, an unknown GitHub event, or nothing set) -> print a reason naming the trigger to stderr and exit non-zero.
2. Merge: read the landed commit's subject (`git log -1 --format=%s <head>`, head = `CICD_HEAD` if set, else `GITHUB_SHA`, else `HEAD`).
   - starts with `chore: bump version` -> do exactly what `cmd_publish()` does (tag + GitHub releases).
   - starts with `chore: install` -> print that nothing is done, exit 0.
   - anything else -> the `cmd_bump()` push path: honour `on_merge` (skip when false), then `handle_push_bump(automerge)` with all its behaviour (no-bump return, `automerge: false` PR, protected-branch fallback, tag + release in the same run after a direct push).
   - the commit before the push is `CICD_BASE` when set, else `GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE` (refactor `handle_push_bump` to take `before` as a parameter or resolve it via a helper; `release bump` must still read `GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE` and fail the same way when unset).
3. Manual: `handle_dispatch_bump(automerge)` reading `CICD_INPUT_BUMP_TYPE`, `CICD_INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY`, `CICD_INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION` when set, else `INPUT_BUMP_TYPE` (default `patch`), `INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY`, `INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION` as today.
4. `release bump` and `release publish` behave exactly as before.
5. Update the module docstring (lines ~1-30, the env var table listing `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`, `GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE`, `GITHUB_SHA`, `INPUT_*`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_REF`) with the no-subcommand mode and the `CICD_*` variables, and the usage line in `main()`.

## Decisions (recorded during refinement)
- Trigger source precedence: `CICD_TRIGGER` wins over `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME` whenever it is set, because inside a git-cicd job running on GitHub Actions both are set and git-cicd's value is the one that describes the job. Same rule for `CICD_BASE` over `GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE`, `CICD_HEAD` over `GITHUB_SHA`, `CICD_INPUT_*` over `INPUT_*`.
- `sync_branch()` takes the branch from `CICD_TARGET_BRANCH` when set, else `GITHUB_REF` as today: git-cicd sets `CICD_TARGET_BRANCH` and the job may run for a branch other than the one in `GITHUB_REF` on a manual run. Unset -> behaviour unchanged.
- The commit-message rule tests the subject line (`%s`) with a prefix match, equivalent to the workflow's `startsWith(head_commit.message, ...)`.
- Auth: the git-cicd merge/manual templates (`.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/templates/workflows/merge.yml` ~line 170, `manual.yml` ~line 185) pass `GITHUB_TOKEN`, not `GH_TOKEN`; `gh` accepts either, so no code change is needed — mention in the docstring that `gh` reads `GH_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`.
- The existing test `TestMain.test_no_subcommand_exits` (tests/test_bump_and_release.py line 640) asserts that no subcommand exits; it can no longer hold unchanged. Replace it with a test that no subcommand and no trigger variables exits non-zero with a reason (the same observable outcome for an un-configured call), and explain the change in the PR description, as the acceptance criteria allow.

## Tests (tests/test_bump_and_release.py, following the existing `mock_run` / `env` fixture and monkeypatch patterns of `TestCmdBump`, `TestCmdPublish`, `TestMain`; no network)
Add a test class for the no-subcommand entry point covering:
- git-cicd merge, landed commit `chore: bump version ...` -> tag push + releases (publish path), no bump-all.
- git-cicd merge, landed commit `chore: install git-semver v0.0.15 (#88)` -> nothing run beyond reading the subject, exit 0.
- git-cicd merge, ordinary commit, files changed -> `bump-all --since <CICD_BASE> --no-push`, push, tag, releases.
- merge, ordinary commit, no configured file changed -> no bump, no push, no tag.
- merge with `on_merge: false` -> skipped.
- merge with `automerge: false` -> PR created from `chore/bump-version-*`, no push.
- merge where direct push hits protected-branch error -> PR fallback, no tag.
- git-cicd manual with each input: `CICD_INPUT_BUMP_TYPE` (patch/minor/major), `CICD_INPUT_SUBDIRECTORY`, `CICD_INPUT_CHANGELOG_DESCRIPTION`; and default `patch` when unset.
- GitHub-only variables (`GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=push` + `GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE`, and `workflow_dispatch` + `INPUT_*`) give the same results.
- `CICD_TRIGGER` precedence over `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME`.
- `CICD_TRIGGER=open` and `CICD_TRIGGER=cron` -> non-zero exit with a reason; nothing run.
- merge with neither `CICD_BASE` nor `GITHUB_EVENT_BEFORE` -> error, non-zero.
- `sync_branch` uses `CICD_TARGET_BRANCH` when set.
All other existing tests pass unmodified. Coverage must not drop (`pytest tests/ -v --cov --cov-report=term-missing`).

## Docs
- `README.md` section `## GitHub Actions` (`### version-bump.yml (Bump & Release)`, ~line 290): add a short subsection describing `release` with no subcommand: the decision rule (bump commit -> publish, install commit -> nothing, else bump; manual -> bump with inputs), the `CICD_*` / GitHub variable precedence, and that `open`/`cron` are refused. Keep the existing `bump`/`publish` description (version-bump.yml still uses them).
- `docs/README.md` if it indexes README sections.

## Out of scope
- `install.sh` and `templates/github/workflows/version-bump.yml` unchanged (install.sh line 95 `install_workflow "version-bump.yml"` stays). `.github/workflows/version-bump.yml` is vendor-protected: do not touch.
- Changing the `latest` tag; replacing `gh`; per-repo publishing.

## Acceptance criteria
- `release` with no subcommand does the right thing for each case above, shown by tests, including bump-commit-publishes, install-commit-does-nothing, no-configured-file-changed-no-bump, `automerge: false`, and a manual run with each input.
- `open`/`cron` refused with a reason and non-zero exit.
- `release bump` / `release publish` unchanged in behaviour; existing tests pass unmodified except `test_no_subcommand_exits`, whose change is explained in the PR.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check` passes; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

title: git-semver released: read-only command printing the version tags released at a commit
body:
## Goal
A repository's own later step in the same release job (e.g. `"steps": [".vendored/pkg/git-semver/release", "ci/publish-image.sh"]`) must be able to tell whether this run released a version, and which, without a token or network. Per-repo publishing (PyPI, images) is not git-semver's business; git-semver's publish stays tag + GitHub release. Planning doc: `.pearls/docs/epics/gsv-81b6.md` (unit 4 of plan `git-dev-883c`; delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`).

## Current code (validated 2026-11-28)
- `git-semver` CLI: `build_parser()` (~line 660) with subparsers `version`, `check`, `bump`, `bump-all`, `tag`; dispatch dict in `main()` (~line 722).
- Tags are formatted by `format_tag(version, subdir=None)` (line 348): `v<version>` for root, `<subdir>/v<version>` for subdirectory components.
- `cmd_tag` (line 592) always moves the `latest` tag (`git tag -f latest`); `release`'s `create_releases()` (line 128) lists `git tag --points-at HEAD` and skips `latest`.

## What to build
A new subcommand in `git-semver`: `git-semver released [<ref>]` (default `HEAD`).
- Prints each version tag pointing at the commit, one per line, sorted, exactly as the tag name (`v0.0.16`, `backend/v2.3.0`).
- A version tag is one matching `v<semver>` or `<subdir>/v<semver>` (the shapes `format_tag` produces). Never prints `latest` or any other non-version tag.
- Prints nothing and exits 0 when no version tag points at the commit.
- Uses only the local repository (`git tag --points-at <ref>` via the existing `git()` helper): no token, no network, no config file required.
- Non-existent `<ref>` -> error message to stderr, non-zero exit.

## Decisions (recorded during refinement)
- Lives in `git-semver` (new subcommand `released`), not in `release`: it is a read-only query like `version`/`check`, needs no CI env, and is callable from a consumer's step as `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/git-semver released`.
- Prints full tag names rather than bare versions, because in a monorepo bare versions are ambiguous between components; for a single-root repo the tag is `v<version>`.
- Optional `<ref>` argument (default HEAD) so a step can ask about `$CICD_HEAD` explicitly; small, no extra surface.

## Tests
- `tests/test_commands.py`: add `TestCmdReleased` following the patterns of `TestCmdVersion` / `TestCmdCheck` (fixtures `make_config`, `mock_git`, `tmp_repo` from `tests/conftest.py`). Cover: tagged commit prints the version tag; commit with `latest` only prints nothing, exit 0; untagged commit prints nothing, exit 0; root + subdir tags at the same commit both printed; non-version tag (e.g. `foo`) ignored; explicit ref argument; bad ref -> non-zero. At least one test runs against a real temporary git repo (`tmp_repo`) to show it needs no network.
- Parser test if the existing suite has one for subcommands.

## Docs
- `README.md` `## Commands`: add `### git-semver released [<ref>]` next to `### git-semver tag [--push]` (~line 130), same style.
- `README.md`: show the later-step pattern — a git-cicd job whose steps are git-semver's release then the repository's own script, e.g. config `"steps": [".vendored/pkg/git-semver/release", "ci/publish-image.sh"]` and a `ci/publish-image.sh` that does `tags=$(.vendored/pkg/git-semver/git-semver released); [ -z "$tags" ] && exit 0` before publishing. State that with a protected branch the publish step sees a version on the run for the merged bump commit, not on the run that opened the bump pull request. Uses `release` with no subcommand (from gsv-81b6.1).

## Out of scope
- No change to `install.sh`, `templates/github/workflows/version-bump.yml`, or the `latest` tag.

## Acceptance criteria
- `git-semver released` prints the version tag(s) at a tagged commit and nothing (exit 0) at an untagged one, with no network; never prints `latest`.
- Tests above pass; coverage does not drop.
- README documents the command and the later-step pattern including the protected-branch note.
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check` passes; `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.

title: Run git-semver's own release as a git-cicd release job (merge on main + manual with inputs)
body:
## Goal
git-semver dogfoods the one-step release: its git-cicd config declares a `release` job that runs on merge to `main` and by hand, so the release decision no longer lives in a workflow file. Planning doc: `.pearls/docs/epics/gsv-81b6.md` (unit 4 of plan `git-dev-883c`; delivers into `plan/git-dev-883c`). Depends on gsv-81b6.1 (`release` with no subcommand).

## Current state (validated 2026-11-28)
- `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` has jobs `test` (on `open`, setup `ci/setup.sh`, steps `ci/test.sh`) and `vendor-check` (on `open`, steps `.vendored/check`) plus a `needs_nothing` list (`*.md`, `LICENSE`, `docs/**`, `commands/*.md`, `.pearls/issues.jsonl`, `.pearls/archive/**`, `.pearls/docs/**`, `.madreperla/sessions.jsonl`).
- git-cicd v0.0.4 at `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd`: job fields `name`, `on`, `branches`, `paths`, `setup`, `steps`, `cron`, `manual`, `blocking`, `inputs`; inputs are `name -> {description, required, default, choices}`; each declared input reaches scripts as `CICD_INPUT_<NAME>`; triggers `open`, `merge`, `cron`, plus `manual`. Generated workflows: `.github/workflows/git-cicd-merge.yml` (Merge), `git-cicd-manual.yml` (Manual), alongside the existing `git-cicd-open.yml`. Its merge/manual templates give the job `contents: write`, `pull-requests: write`, checkout `fetch-depth: 0`, `fetch-tags: true`, and pass `GITHUB_TOKEN`; runs are serialized without a concurrency group.
- Only `.github/workflows/git-cicd-open.yml` exists today; `.github/workflows/version-bump.yml` (vendor-protected via `_vendor.protected` in `.vendored/configs/git-semver.json`) still runs `release bump`/`release publish`.

## What to build
1. Add a `release` job to `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json`:
   - `"on": ["merge"]`, `"branches": ["main"]`, `"paths": ["**"]`, manual runs allowed (default), `inputs`: `bump_type` (choices `patch`, `minor`, `major`; default `patch`), `subdirectory` (optional), `changelog_description` (optional), declared the way git-cicd's own config (`mangimangi/git-cicd` `.vendored/configs/git-cicd.json` / its release job) declares them.
   - Step runs this repository's own root `release` (e.g. `"steps": ["release"]`), NOT `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/release`, which lacks the new entry point until a release is installed back — the same way git-cicd's workflow runs its own root tool.
   - No `ci/` wrapper: `release` reads `CICD_*` itself after gsv-81b6.1.
2. Run `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd generate`; commit the generated `.github/workflows/git-cicd-merge.yml` and `git-cicd-manual.yml` with the (possibly regenerated) `git-cicd-open.yml`. Do not hand-edit them.
3. Verify the bump commit's files (VERSION / CHANGELOG under `.semver/` or wherever the config writes them) are not all matched by `needs_nothing`; if a bump commit would be classified as needing nothing, the publish path would never run — adjust the job (or document) so `chore: bump version` merges still run `release`.
4. Docs:
   - `README.md` and `AGENTS.md`: how a release happens in this repo (git-cicd `release` job on merge to `main`; bump commit -> tag + GitHub release) and how to start one by hand (Actions tab, **Manual**, job `release`, with `bump_type`/`subdirectory`/`changelog_description`). Update the AGENTS.md Key Files table (`release` row: called by the git-cicd `release` job; add `git-cicd-merge.yml`/`git-cicd-manual.yml`) and the README `### Pull request checks` area (~line 375) / a new release subsection.
   - README section for adopters (`## GitHub Actions`, ~line 290): document the git-cicd `merge` job that replaces `version-bump.yml` for a repository using git-cicd (config snippet with `.vendored/pkg/git-semver/release` as step and the three inputs), next to the existing `version-bump.yml` docs, stating that `version-bump.yml` stays the default install.

## Decisions (recorded during refinement)
- `.vendored/configs/git-semver.json` `files` is unchanged: no new file ships to consumers (no `ci/` wrapper is needed, `release` is already listed). The doc listed `files` only as possibly affected.
- `paths: ["**"]`: the release job must see every merge; whether a bump is needed is `git-semver bump-all`'s decision, not git-cicd's path filter.
- On the integration branch the old `version-bump.yml` and the new job will both exist and both react to merges; this is accepted by the plan (the planning session removes `version-bump.yml` before the branch reaches `main`). Do not add, change or delete `version-bump.yml` or `dogfood.yml`.

## Out of scope
- `install.sh`, `templates/github/workflows/version-bump.yml` unchanged; no consumer migration; no change in git-cicd or git-vendored; vendored files under `.vendored/pkg/` untouched.

## Acceptance criteria
- `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd validate` reports the `release` job; `git-cicd verify` passes (generated workflows match config); `.vendored/pkg/git-cicd/git-cicd check --setup` passes.
- Generated Merge and Manual workflows committed with Open.
- README and AGENTS.md describe the in-repo release and the manual run; README documents the adopter merge job next to `version-bump.yml`.
- PR into `plan/git-dev-883c` has a passing `Verdict / git-cicd:verdict`.
- `python3 .vendored/check --base origin/plan/git-dev-883c` reports nothing.
